title: Photon-Counting Computed Tomography (PCCT) for Coronary Assessment in Patients with Acute Chest Pain: A Registry Study
summary:
Coronary heart disease remains the most common cause of death of any kind worldwide. Coronary angiography is the central component in both the diagnosis and treatment of coronary heart disease and its consequences such as vascular constriction and acute heart attack. However, important limitations remained, especially with regard to the extraluminal characterization of narrowings and plaques, which can only be partially overcome with intravascular imaging. Plaque composition and characterization play a crucial role for patients, including with regard to future events.

Over the last few years, CT angiography has developed further and new methods such as photon counting CT have greatly improved the difficult imaging of the coronary vessels. In particular, there is the possibility of complete characterization of coronary (extravascular) plaques including calcification, anatomy, degree of stenosis and high-risk features.

In the planned registry study, patients with an increased pretest probability of coronary heart disease should receive a PCCT examination before the gold standard coronary angiography for the detection of coronary narrowings and plaque characteristics as part of the necessarily indicated and guideline-based diagnostics and therapy. Furthermore, subjective and objective parameters for image quality as well as the radiation dose applied during both examinations in comparison to conventional multi-slice CT systems as well as clinical data should be collected.

interventions.name: The study will assess patients, who are referred to the hospital for cardiac evaluation due to suspected acute coronary syndrome. The patient population will only include clinically stable patients with intermediate and low risk NSTEMI (non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction) or unstable ang

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Patients with acute chest pain and clinically suspected significant CAD (low to intermediate-risk NSTEMI or unstable angina according to internal SOP and GRACE-Score risk stratification) with requirement of diagnostic angiography.
-	Age >18 years 
-	Ability to perform a breath hold of 15 s
-	Negative serum pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential
-	Signing of informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
-	STEMI-typical changes in the ECG or criteria for high or very high risk NSTEMI
-	History of allergy to iodinated contrast media
-	Renal insufficiency (GFR < 50 ml/min)
-	Hyperthyroidism
-	Pharmacologic or mechanical inotropic support (excluding digoxin)
-	Heart rate above 80/min and contraindications to beta blockers (hypotension, obstructive airway disease)
